assessment_summary: The statement claims that every connected 3-regular graph has a perfect matching, meaning the bridgeless condition in Petersen's theorem is unnecessary. This is false. A standard counterexample can be constructed by connecting three odd components (each having exactly one vertex of degree 2 and the rest degree 3, such as a K_4 with one subdivided edge) to a single central vertex. The resulting graph is a connected 3-regular graph, but removing the central vertex leaves 3 odd components, violating Tutte's condition for the existence of a perfect matching.
counterexample: A graph formed by taking three copies of a graph with 5 vertices and degrees 3,3,3,3,2 (e.g., K_4 with one edge subdivided) and connecting their degree-2 vertices to a single central vertex. This 3-regular graph has no perfect matching because removing the central vertex leaves 3 odd components.
